title: Development Exit Loans UK
h1: Not revealed by search results. Indexed link title is "Development Exit Loans UK" [a][b].
summary: Silver Oak Capital's Development Exit Loans page (indexed title "Development Exit Loans UK") presents a development exit loan as a short-term bridging loan secured on a completed or nearly completed development, used to redeem / pay off the existing construction (development) lender. It typically gives the developer roughly 12 to 18 months to sell, with repayments made as each unit sells. Stated reasons to use it: avoid default penalties / default interest (which can roughly double the rate) when the development loan nears expiry, avoid discounting units to sell quickly, and release equity early for the next project. The page says it is cheaper than construction finance because construction risk has fallen away. No lender list, fee schedule, LTV range, process steps, CTA wording or meta description for this page were revealed. Related Silver Oak pages surfaced: FAQ (development loans usually run 18-24 months; exit bridge gives a further 12 months at a lower rate), a bridging guide (exit finance as fallback adding 12 to 24 months), and the NW London case study (GBP 19m, 0.75% per month, 12 months, max 73% LTV, 15% personal guarantee; deal-specific, not general pricing). The direct page could not be fetched; all content is from search-tool summaries of the indexed page.

sections.heading: What a development exit loan is (page content as summarised by search [a][b])
sections.content: A short-term bridging loan secured on a completed or nearly completed development, used to pay off the existing construction lender / redeem the original development facility. It typically gives the borrower roughly 12 to 18 months to sell, with repayments made as each unit sells.

sections.heading: Why developers use it (page content as summarised by search [a][b])
sections.content: Avoid default penalties when a development loan nears expiry: construction loans near expiry may attract default interest, which can roughly double the rate; refinancing before that point can move the borrower to a lower rate. Avoid discounting units to sell quickly. Release equity early for the next project.

sections.heading: Cost angle (page content as summarised by search [a])
sections.content: The page says a development exit loan is cheaper than construction finance, since construction risk has already fallen away.
